scenes.desc: Uno de los dos grandes grupos de Pye a principios de 1966. «Till the End of the Day» era uno de los tres discos duros del Top 10 británico de enero.

podcast.title: Brief Member of The Rolling Stones
podcast.body: Mick Avory was a member of The Rolling Stones for "a very brief period." He chose to quit before Charlie Watts joined, as he "didn't want to be a full-time drummer" at that time. Upon the Stones' subsequent success, he "realised his mistake" and sought another band. "Avery had actually been a member of the Rolling Stones for a very brief period, but had decided he didn't want to be a full-time drummer and had quit before they got Charlie Watson."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Joining The Kinks
podcast.body: Mick Avory was chosen as the permanent drummer for The Kinks by Ray Davis and the management team, after Dave Davis's preferred choice, Viv Prince of The Pretty Things, was unavailable. Despite Dave Davis taking an "instant dislike to him," Avory was accepted as "the best drummer available." "Avery was chosen by Ray and the management team, and Dave Davis took an instant this like to him, partly because Ray liked Avery, but Dave accepted that he was the best drummer available."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Not on Early Studio Recordings
podcast.body: Despite joining The Kinks as their permanent drummer, Mick Avory "wouldn't play on the next few records." Producer Shell Tauhmey preferred to use musicians he already knew, and Avory was considered "a bit of an unknown quantity" in the studio. However, he was available for the group's "first big tour" (with The Dave Clark Five and The Hollies) and their "first TV appearance" on Ready Steady Go. "Avery wouldn't play on the next few records. Tommie liked to use musicians he knew, and Avery was a bit of an unknown quantity."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
